Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association (MMA)
Neither For Nor Against
LD 288, An Act to Make Technical Changes to Maine 's Tax Laws
February 27, 2025

Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee
on Taxation, my name is Amanda Campbell, and I am submitting testimony on behalf of the Maine Municipal Association's 70-member Legislative Policy Committee (LPC) neither for nor against LD 288.

Municipal officials, especially assessors, have concerns and questions about Section A-l which seeks to
amend 36 MRSA �327, sub-�3, by changing the language used to determine if a noncertified assessor is
qualified. Current law describes this official as having been, "professionally trained" while the proposed language is vaguer, requiring the individual to have, "the basic knowledge required to perform the
assessing function."

How does an individual prove this basic knowledge and regarding what function of the assessing
practice? Municipal officials fear that this change in language, while appearing to be semantics, could in fact decrease the quality and knowledge of professionals in the assessing industry. There is no doubt that the number of assessors in Maine is decreasing, but trading quality for quantity is never best practice.

This session has already shown that property taxes and assessment are at the top of many peop1e's minds.

Questions about assessment practices and the entire taxation process are asked of municipal officials

I daily. Dozens of bills have already been introduced attempting to address this issue.

-

Instead of amending language that could potentially harm the property taxpayers, let's all work together to
streamline the process of reviewing property tax practice reforms.

Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you and share the municipal perspective on this important
topic. Please feel free to contact me or any member of the MMA Advocacy team with any questions
related to municipal operations.

TESTIMONY OF DANIEL D'ALESSANDRO, DEPUTY TAX POLICY COUNSEL DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation Hearing Date: February 27, 2025
LD 288 -- "An Act to Make Technical Changes to Maine's Tax Laws"
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and members of the Taxation
Committee -- good afternoon, my name is Daniel D'Alessandro, Deputy Tax Policy
Counsel for the Office of Tax Policy in the Department of Administrative and
Financial Sen/ices. I am testifying at the request of the Administration in Support
of LD 288 "An Act to Make Technical Changes to Maine's Tax Laws."
This bill was drafted and submitted by the Department of Administrative and Financial Services, Maine Revenue Services. Each year, Maine Revenue Services and the Office of Tax Policy prepare one or more bills that propose changes to various existing provisions of Maine law; primarily to Title 36. The purpose of this bill is to make certain technical improvements and clarifications in Maine's tax law
consistent with current tax administration.
The Department has also submitted another bill: LD 68 - "An Act to Amend
the State Tax Laws." These bills differ in the nature of the Department's
recommendations. While LD 68, the "Act to Amend," contains substantive
changes, this bill contains technical, non-substantive amendments to Maine's tax laws. These changes have no impact on the tax receipts included in recent baseline revenue forecasts by the Revenue Forecasting Committee.
The changes in this bill are designed to improve the clarity and
administration of the current law. This includes changes to clarify statutory
1

language consistent with ongoing administrative practice, removing and replacing gendered language, improving and updating syntax and grammar, harmonizing
certain changes made by the Legislature last session, repealing expired provisions, and making other technical and grammatical changes to improve existing statutory
language.

provision of the bill, including a proposed amendment, and matches it with the corresponding paragraph from the bill's summary section. This side-by-side chart provides a brief explanation of each provision of the bill.

and leaseback of machinery and equipment. Potential unintended consequences
with this change have been raised and we would ask the Committee to remove the
provision.

Testimony in Opposition to
LD 288 An Act to Make Technical Changes to Maine's Tax Laws
March 5, 2025
Chairpersons Senator Grohoski and Representative Cloutier and honorable members of the Taxation Committee:
My name is Kerry Leichtman. I am a Certified Maine Assessor serving the jurisdictions of Camden and Rockport and am writing you today in opposition to LD 288.
LD 288 suggests four changes to Maine's tax laws, two of which I can support (numbers 2 & 3), one that I don't understand (number 4) and one that I strongly oppose (number 1).
I'll confine my comment to Change #1: "requiring fulltime property assessors to be certified by Maine Revenue Services as having "the basic knowledge required to perform the assessing function" rather than certified as "professionally trained assessors."
I am not sure how MRS can "certify" that fulltime property assessors have "the basic knowledge required to perform the assessing function" without certifying them as professionally trained assessors. The verbal gymnastics of that sentence leaves much to interpretation.
My interpretation of it is that the standards assessors are held to are to be reduced. This job gets more difficult and complex each year. I get it that there is currently a shortage of assessors but lessening the standards is not how to deal with it a very complicated job.
I am the full-time assessor for two towns. I could not do this without excellent assistance in both towns. I think Camden and Rockport are well served by this arrangement, and I think it is a better way to deal with the assessor shortage than lowering the standards. I'm sorry I cannot be at the hearing today to discuss this with you as I have an all day obligation that I cannot reschedule.
Should you decide to schedule a work session on this bill, I'd be pleased to participate should you desire it.
Thank you for considering these comments.
